jobs.description:
Chief Operating Officer

**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**Reports to**

Chief Executive Officer

**Classification**

Full\-time, exempt

**Leadership role**

Member of the Senior Leadership Team

**Location**

Transylvania County, North Carolina; regular travel to program and project sites

Position Summary

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the chief executive's principal partner for translating strategy into disciplined, effective day\-to\-day operations. The COO provides organization\-wide leadership for people, processes, systems, compliance, and performance management so that Transylvania Habitat for Humanity (THFH) can serve more families while maintaining quality, stewardship, and an excellent homeowner, volunteer, donor, customer, and employee experience.

Working across departments, the COO strengthens coordination among affordable homeownership, critical home repair and aging in place, disaster recovery, volunteer engagement, finance and administration, ReStore operations, and marketing and advertising. The COO leads through collaboration, clear expectations, measurable results, and continuous improvement.

Essential Responsibilities

**Operational Leadership and Execution:** Convert the strategic plan and annual priorities into coordinated operating plans, clear accountabilities, measurable goals, and reliable follow\-through.

· Lead annual and quarterly operating planning in partnership with the CEO and department leaders; monitor progress and resolve barriers that cross departmental lines.

· Establish practical performance dashboards, workflows, service standards, and meeting rhythms that support timely decisions and organizational accountability.

· Evaluate and improve policies, procedures, technology, documentation, and internal controls as THFH grows in scale and complexity.

· Balance immediate operational needs with long\-range capacity, financial sustainability, risk management, and mission impact.

**Homeowner and Community Services:** Provide direct leadership and supervision to the Homeowner Services and Critical Repair Departments and ensure coordinated, equitable, and compliant service delivery.

· Oversee the systems supporting homeowner outreach, application, eligibility, selection, education, partnership, mortgage readiness, closing, and post\-purchase support.

· Ensure strong coordination of Critical Home Repair, Aging in Place, disaster recovery, case navigation, and neighborhood\-based initiatives, including clear eligibility standards and complete records.

· Promote a respectful, trauma\-informed, and customer\-centered experience for applicants, homeowners, and community residents.

· Track program outputs, outcomes, waitlists, cycle times, and client feedback; use data to improve service and allocate resources.

**Cross\-Functional Program Delivery:** Create reliable handoffs and shared accountability from land acquisition and funding through construction, family readiness, sale, and long\-term stewardship.

· Partner with the CEO, QLO, Construction Director, finance staff, Resource Development, and Homeowner Services team to align the development pipeline, project schedules, budgets, grant commitments, and closing requirements.

· Support effective delivery of new construction, repair, disaster recovery, and community development initiatives without duplicating the Construction Director's technical authority.

· Identify capacity constraints and operational risks early; recommend solutions, assign ownership, and ensure resolution.

· Coordinate organizational response during disasters, urgent client situations, or other complex operational events as directed by the CEO.

**People and Culture:** Build a healthy, accountable, collaborative workplace in which staff understand how their work advances THFH's mission.

· Supervise assigned department leaders; set goals, provide coaching and feedback, conduct performance evaluations, and support professional development.

· Partner with the CEO and appropriate staff on workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, compensation administration, employee relations, succession planning, and consistent application of personnel policies.

· Clarify roles and decision rights, strengthen communication across teams, and address performance or conflict promptly and fairly.

· Model integrity, humility, inclusion, sound judgment, and respect for the contributions of employees, volunteers, homeowners, and community partners.

**Financial Stewardship, Compliance, and Risk:** Partner with the CEO and finance leadership to safeguard THFH's resources and maintain strong operational controls.

· Participate in annual budgeting, forecasting, cash\-flow and capacity planning, and regular review of departmental and program performance against budget.

· Ensure that operational practices support accurate grant tracking, contract compliance, mortgage and closing requirements, insurance obligations, safety standards, and applicable Habitat for Humanity policies.

· Maintain current, usable policies and procedures; promote consistent documentation, confidentiality, records retention, and data quality.

· Support audit readiness, corrective actions, business continuity, and responsible management of organizational risk.

**ReStore and Volunteer Engagement:** Support strong mission integration, operational discipline, and community engagement across revenue\-generating and volunteer\-supported activities.

· Work with ReStore leadership to monitor business plans, customer and donor experience, safety, staffing, inventory practices, sales performance, and contribution to THFH's mission.

· Strengthen volunteer recruitment, orientation, scheduling, training, recognition, retention, and deployment across construction, repair, ReStore, committees, and special events.

· Encourage effective use of volunteers while maintaining appropriate staff oversight, safety, quality, and meaningful engagement.

jobs.description:
**Chief Development Officer**  

*Location: Boys \& Girls Club of the Northern Plains*  

  

Are you a visionary leader ready to make a lasting impact on the lives of young people? Do you have the passion, drive, and expertise to spearhead transformative fundraising initiatives? If so, we want YOU to join our dynamic team as the **Chief Development Officer**!  

  

**About Us:**  

At the Boys \& Girls Club of the Northern Plains, our mission is to inspire and enable all young people, especially those who need us most, to realize their full potential as productive, responsible, and caring citizens. As part of our executive team, you will have a direct influence on advancing this mission by driving fundraising and development strategies that foster positive change in the lives of youth across our region.  

  

**Why You'll Love This Role:**  

As the Chief Development Officer, you'll work alongside our Chief Executive Officer, Board of Directors, and Advisory Councils, playing a key role in shaping the future of our organization. You'll lead a talented team dedicated to fundraising and grant management, and you’ll engage with major donors to help ensure we continue to be a force for good in the community.  

You’ll also have the chance to:

* Develop innovative fundraising strategies, from major gifts to capital campaigns.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, corporations, and foundations.
* Lead grant management efforts to secure vital resources.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* **Leadership**: Guide the Resource Development team and act as a visionary for future fundraising initiatives.
* **Fundraising**: Drive strategies for major gifts, planned giving, corporate partnerships, and annual campaigns.
* **Grant Management**: Identify and pursue grant opportunities while ensuring compliance with reporting requirements.
* **Administration**: Report progress to the CEO and Board, manage donor records, and ensure reconciliation with the Finance Department.
* **Team Management**: Lead and inspire a team of development and grant professionals.

**What You’ll Bring:**

* A **Bachelor’s degree** is preferred.
* Proven success in **fundraising**, including major gifts, annual campaigns, and grant writing.
* Stellar communication and relationship\-building skills with diverse stakeholders.
* Strong leadership abilities and experience managing a high\-performing team.
* A passion for our mission and a commitment to driving positive change.
* A desire to travel and engage with our communities frequently.

**What We Offer:**

* Health, Dental, Vision, STD \& LTD, Life \& 401k
* Voluntary AFLAC and More!
* PTO, Paid Holidays, Additional Paid Leave after third consecutive year of employment.
* Site Discounts – 50% reduction in cost to Early Childhood Education and Academy programs immediately upon hire
* Relocation Assistance
* Travel Expense Reimbursement
* Hybrid Capabilities
* Bonus / Incentive Opportunities
* Continuing Education Stipend

**Join Us:**  

This is more than just a job—it’s a chance to lead with purpose and drive meaningful change. If you're ready to take on a leadership role that makes a difference in the lives of youth while developing a successful career, apply today to become our **Chief Development Officer**.  

  

Help us continue to inspire greatness in the next generation. **Apply now!**  

  

**POLICY ON PLACEMENT AND RECRUITING**  

The Boys \& Girls Club of the Northern Plains are equal opportunity\-employers committed to the principles of non\-discrimination in the workplace. Candidates will not be discriminated against based on age, race, creed, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, marital status, or any other basis that is prohibited by federal, state, or local law.

**Position Purpose:**  

  

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for the overall operational leadership, strategic execution, and financial performance of the catering organization. This position oversees all aspects of catering production, event operations, logistics, purchasing, warehousing, transportation, staffing, and customer service to ensure the company consistently delivers exceptional events and experiences. The COO is responsible for translating the organization's strategic vision into effective operational plans that drive growth, profitability, operational excellence, and customer satisfaction. The COO develops and maintains efficient systems, processes, and performance standards that maximize productivity, control costs, ensure regulatory compliance, and support the organization's long\-term success.  

  

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**  

* Lead and oversee all company operations, including culinary production, event execution, logistics, warehousing, transportation, purchasing, and customer service.


* Partner with the Chief Executive Officer to develop and execute strategic initiatives, growth plans, and operational objectives that support the organization's vision and long\-term success.


* Identify and pursue new business opportunities, strategic partnerships, and market segments to expand the company's catering footprint, increase revenue, strengthen client relationships, and establish and grow the organization's portfolio of corporate, nonprofit, social, government, and special event clients.


* Negotiate contracts and service agreements with suppliers, vendors, and business partners to maximize value and operational effectiveness.


* Direct the planning, coordination, and execution of catering events to ensure exceptional service, operational efficiency, and client satisfaction.


* Establish, implement, and continuously improve operational systems, policies, procedures, and performance standards to maximize productivity and service quality.


* Develop and manage operating budgets, monitor labor and food costs, and ensure achievement of profitability goals and financial targets.


* Analyze operational and financial performance metrics, identify trends, and implement strategies to improve efficiency, reduce waste, and increase revenue.


* Oversee purchasing, inventory control, supply chain management, and vendor relationships to ensure cost\-effective procurement and uninterrupted operations.


* Oversee recruitment, workforce planning, training, employee development, succession planning, and retention initiatives to build and maintain a high\-performing workforce.


* Foster a culture of excellence, teamwork, accountability, innovation, and customer\-focused service throughout the organization.


* Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including food safety standards, health department requirements, and OSHA regulations.


* Ensure menu planning for residential sites are reviewed by a licensed dietician and meet USDA nutritional standards.
* Direct risk management, workplace safety, emergency preparedness, and quality assurance programs to protect employees, customers, assets, and company reputation.


* Oversee the maintenance, utilization, and replacement of company facilities, fleet vehicles, equipment, and operational assets to ensure readiness and efficiency.


  

**Non\-Essential Duties and Responsibilities**  

* Participate in industry associations, networking events, and community engagement activities.


* Other duties as assigned.


  

**Qualifications:**  

* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Hospitality Management, Culinary Management, Supply Chain Management, or a related field required.


* Minimum of eight (8\) years of progressively responsible leadership experience in catering, hospitality, food service, event management, restaurant operations, or a related industry.


* Minimum of three (3\) years of senior operational leadership experience.


* Extensive knowledge of catering operations, food service management, event execution, supply chain logistics, and hospitality industry best practices.


* Exceptional leadership, communication, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills.


* Knowledge of HACCP, OSHA, food safety regulations, health department standards, and risk management practices.


* Proven ability to lead organizational change and drive operational improvements.


* An attitude compatible with the goals and purposes of NCCF.

  

  

  

**Physical Demands/Work Environment:**  

  

While performing the responsibilities of the job, the employee is required to talk and hear. The employee is often required to sit and use their hands and fingers to handle or feel. The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, reach with arms and hands, climb or balance, and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl. Vision abilities required by this job require close vision working with a computer monitor. While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to sit, stand, walk, speak, hear, and use hands and fingers to operate equipment and technology. The employee may occasionally lift and move items weighing up to 25 pounds. The employee will routinely visit kitchens, warehouses, event venues, and production facilities and may be exposed to varying temperatures, food preparation environments, and event locations. The noise level is typically moderate but may occasionally be loud during production or event activities. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.  

  

**Salary: $67,000 \- $70,000 \+ Incentive based bonuses based on company and contract growth.**

Our intention is to have employees who are passionate about making their personal mission statement come to life each day at work! Be it through providing healing, eradicating loneliness, contributing to efficiencies, streamlining processes, being dependable, sparking creativity or something else, the demonstration of HOW you do your job is just as important as WHAT you do in your job.

  

Alongside our valued employees, we are making a difference throughout the state of Ohio in the lives of those that need healthcare or those embracing the next chapter of their lives. Sustained members of our team demonstrate accountable behavior and share our values of customer service, innovation, integrity, financial stewardship, inclusion, leadership and care.

  

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for operational leadership, strategic planning support, financial and operational results, including quality of services and satisfaction, for the organization and ensures services operate in accordance with federal, state, and local regulatory standards, to ensure that the highest degree of care and services are delivered.

jobs.title: Senior Vice President & Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**Who is the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra?**  

Known for its artistic excellence for more than 130 years, today the PSO is the region’s national and international cultural ambassador. A two\-time 2018 GRAMMY® Award\-winning orchestral ensemble credited with a rich history of concerts, performances, and recordings with the world’s finest conductors and musicians, the PSO consistently demonstrates a genuine commitment to Pittsburgh’s citizens, regional communities, and vibrant cultural scene. The internationally acclaimed Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra (PSO) engages audiences of all ages through unparalleled live musical experiences, community collaborations, and educational programming that enrich every life with great music.  

  

**JOB PURPOSE AND REPORTING STRUCTURE:**  

The Senior Vice President \& Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a key strategic and operational partner with the CEO and other organizational leadership in decision making and fulfilling the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra’s mission and goals. The COO is responsible for executing on annual and long\-term plans of the PSO through leadership and supervision in the following areas: artistic planning, strategic planning, orchestra\-, stage\-, and facility\-operations, electronic media, technology, orchestra personnel, labor relations, community programs, business intelligence, and general operations. The COO is part of the senior leadership team and works closely with the CEO, the CFO, the CDO, the CREO, the Music Director, the Board of Directors and other members of the leadership team on the execution of mission and strategic direction of the organization.  

  

**Direct Reports:** Vice President of Artistic Planning, Vice President of Operations, Vice President of Information Technology, Senior Vice President of Learning \& Engagement, Director of Commercial \& Popular Programming and Executive Administrative Associate.  

  

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITES:**  

Leadership – the COO provides organizational leadership with a focus on daily internal operations as well as partnering with the C\-Suite on strategic planning for the future. The COO provides organizational leadership in the CEO’s absence and is the public face of the organization in the CEO’s absence. The COO provides general oversight of the PSI’s management operating system to ensure that planning processes, management controls, and internal communications effectively deliver the business of the PSI.  

  

Span of Control \- the COO supervises and directs all departments responsible for planning, developing and executing the Symphony seasons, Heinz Hall programming and operations, as well as activities related to education, electronic media and community programs. They work closely with the CFO and CEO on budget development and monitoring as well as long\-range financial planning for operational expenses. The COO also works in conjunction with senior leadership on the development and execution of the strategic plan, community projects, community relationships, run out and tour relationships as well as fundraising and marketing and communications when appropriate.  

  

Capital Projects \- The COO provides executive leadership and oversight for the PSO’s capital projects, ensuring investment strategies align with corporate objectives, operational priorities, growth initiatives, and long\-term financial goals. Direct capital planning and resource allocation processes across departments to maximize return and support sustainable organizational growth. Partner with executive leadership and key stakeholders to develop business cases, assess risks, establish funding priorities, and make strategic decisions regarding major capital investments.  

  

Staff Development and Management – The COO is responsible for ensuring that the departments are staffed appropriately and within the financial forecasts. The COO ensures that performance expectations are clearly defined, measured and if needed addressed. The COO, in conjunction with department leadership, identifies opportunities for employee growth and training. The COO leads the efforts to ensure that the work environment allows staff to perform, thrive and succeed.  

  

Labor Relations – The COO, in conjunction with the CEO, CFO, CREO and VP of Operations, is responsible for the labor relations management on behalf of the Symphony and for developing and maintaining collaborative working relationships with the labor unions working within the organization. This includes working closely with the VP of Operations and CREO on regular contract management, grievance processes and the collective bargaining negotiations process with seven unions. The COO ensures that the collective bargaining processes are aligned with the organizational direction strategies and goals. The COO also works with the CEO, VP of Operations and Director of Orchestra Personnel on individual contract negotiations with PSO musicians.  

  

**QUALIFICATIONS:*** College degree required, advanced degree and musical background preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of increasing responsibility in operational leadership and strategic planning.
* At least 8 years of experience in arts management, preferably in orchestra management.
* At least 5 years of experience in a senior management role with a professional arts organization.
* Demonstrated experience in motivating, managing and developing teams.
* Experience with large capital projects.
* Experience with labor negotiations and collective bargaining agreements.
* Working knowledge of orchestra repertoire and orchestra operations.

**Compensation and Location:**  

This is a full\-time exempt position with an annual salary between $200,000 \- $270,000 depending upon experience. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package which includes paid holidays, paid time off, employer paid health benefits, as well as retirement savings options with an employer match. jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer / Integrator
jobs.description:
**Turbo Tim’s is growing, and we need a COO who can help turn big ideas into a great company at scale.**

**I’m Turbo Tim. In EOS and Rocket Fuel terms, I’m the textbook Visionary. I see possibilities everywhere, move fast, and love trying things the automotive industry hasn’t tried. I need a true Integrator beside me: someone who loves people, brings clarity to complexity, makes decisions, builds strong leaders, and turns ideas into results. You’ll be empowered to lead the business and tell me when an idea needs a better plan.**

**We’re an independent, multi\-location automotive company built around Cars, Cats, and Community. We’re expanding quickly, building a YouTube channel that shows what shop life can be, and developing a software company aimed at improving this industry. Depending on your strengths and interests, you could help shape those ventures too. We put on community events like Car Extravaganza and Crushawhirl, and our team volunteers because giving back is part of who we are. There’s a lot happening here, and the right person will help us grow it without losing what makes it special.**

**Our values are Care, CommUNITY, Trust, Innovation, and FUN. They have to show up in how we treat customers, develop employees, solve problems, and make decisions. We take employee feedback seriously: we track eNPS, listen to what drives it, and keep changing how we work to make this a better place for our people.**

**What you’ll own**
-------------------

* **Lead day\-to\-day operations across our locations and help build the systems, accountability, and leadership capacity needed for continued growth.**
* **Be the Integrator: turn vision into priorities, align the leadership team, follow through, and help us decide what deserves our attention now.**
* **Coach and grow our leaders. Build a company where people know what success looks like and have the support to reach it.**
* **Own operational performance and work with the team to improve the customer experience, financial results, and execution across the business.**
* **Use EOS tools and a healthy leadership cadence to surface issues, make decisions, and keep us moving.**
* **Protect and strengthen our culture as we add people, locations, and new ventures.**

**You might be our person if**
------------------------------

* **You’ve led people and operations through meaningful growth, and you can balance big\-picture thinking with consistent follow\-through.**
* **You understand EOS and the Visionary/Integrator relationship in Rocket Fuel, ideally because you’ve lived it.**
* **You’re direct, kind, calm under pressure, and genuinely good at getting the best out of people.**
* **You can challenge a passionate founder, earn trust across a team, and make ambitious ideas executable.**
* **You’re excited to bring a fresh perspective to automotive. Experience outside the automotive industry is especially welcome.**
* **You care about culture and employee feedback as much as you care about a scorecard.**

**Our previous COO has been an amazing Integrator and person. He set a high bar. At times we wondered how we could possibly offer him more room to grow, and he kept growing anyway. Those are big shoes to fill. You won’t be expected to fill them alone: we’ll support your development, give you room to lead, and expect you to invest just as deeply in the growth of our people.**

**If you want to lead a company that’s growing fast, trying new things, and doing real good in the community, we’d love to meet you. Apply with your résumé and a short note about why the Visionary/Integrator partnership appeals to you.**

jobs.title: Executive Director, Chief Operations Officer - Aetna Better Health of Maryland
jobs.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

**Position Summary**


Aetna Better Health is Aetna’s Medicaid managed care plan. Backed by over 30 years of experience managing the care of those with a broad array of health care needs, our Medicaid plans have demonstrated that getting the right help when you need it is essential to better health. That’s why Aetna® Medicaid plans include the guidance and support needed to connect our members with the right coverage, resources, and care. We are focused on enhancing quality and population health outcomes while integrating CVS assets to bring accessible healthcare to our members.

  

Aetna Better Health of Maryland is seeking an experience leader with vast operational knowledge of Medicaid for its state\-wide managed Medicaid business in the role of Chief Operations Officer (COO). The COO role will be strategic and committed to developing colleagues as well as relentlessly pursuing change that is best for the organization and its customers. The COO role will collaborate with the CEO to develop the strategic vision of the Health Plan, policies \& procedures, and operational objectives including leading RFP readiness efforts. The COO will oversee high level strategic and operational activities of various plan functional areas which include traditional service operations (Claims, Provider Services, Information Technology, Grievance \& Appeals and Member Services) as well as Medical Management (Quality, Network, Compliance, Health Equity, Medical Directors, Utilization Management, Vendor Management). These activities may include colleague productivity, building and maintaining a highly inclusive and diverse culture as well as ensuring team members thrive and organizational outcomes are met.

 **Major Responsibilities**

* Partner with the Plan CEO to drive successful growth, operational excellence, and overall business performance.
* Oversee financial management of the health plan, including budget accountability, revenue target achievement, and P\&L performance.
* Collaborate with corporate functional leaders and centralized shared services teams to drive operational effectiveness and business results.
* Provide leadership and oversight across core operational areas, including: Claims systems and processing, Third\-Party Liability (TPL) and Coordination of Benefits (COB), Pharmacy claims operations and their impact on total cost of care, Call center operations and performance and Encounter data management and processing.
* Lead and support provider operations activities, including: Provider data management, Credentialing, Provider relations, Network development and contracting, and Value\-based care contracting and performance initiatives.
* Drive strategies that enhance provider experience while managing medical costs and improving operational outcomes.
* Ensure compliance with all applicable state contracts, regulations, executive orders, and healthcare industry requirements.
* Partner with Government Affairs and Legal teams to address regulatory, legislative, and compliance\-related matters.
* Serve as a key advocate with internal stakeholders, state regulators, policymakers, and other external partners.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with community\-based advocacy organizations and industry stakeholders.
* Oversee communications and engagement strategies for members and providers.
* Support and promote community\-based programs that address Social Determinants of Health (SDOH), including housing, employment, Community Health Workers (CHWs), Peer support specialists and nutrition and food access initiatives.
* Apply expertise in the integration of physical and behavioral healthcare, with a strong understanding of the unique needs of the Medicaid population.
* Represent the organization externally with regulatory agencies, state departments, community partners, and other key stakeholders.
* Act as a trusted executive leader and extension of the CEO, providing strategic leadership both internally and externally.

  

The COO will oversee business operations performance and employee productivity, building and maintaining our highly inclusive and diverse culture, ensuring team members thrive, and organizational outcomes are met. Lead people, build/maintain relationships while driving talent and culture development.

 **Required Qualifications**


The candidate will have a strong work ethic, be a self\-starter, and be able to be highly productive in a dynamic, collaborative environment. This position offers broad exposure to all aspects of the company’s business, as well as significant interaction with all the business leaders. The candidate will be expected to have the following key attributes:

  

* 10\+ years of work experience reflecting a proven track record of government programs such as Medicaid, Medicare, or Dual Eligible plans.
* 5\+ years of experience in executive leadership roles with proven track record of proficiency in the operational competencies noted.
* Demonstrated success with C\-suite stakeholders.
* Ability to work collaboratively across many teams, prioritize demands from those teams, synthesize information received, and generate meaningful conclusions.
* Ability to conceive innovative ideas or solutions to meet clients’ requirements.
* Excellent communication and relationship management skills and being able to express thoughts in an organized and articulate manner.
* Ability to build a climate of trust and respect with regulators, external stakeholders, as well as colleagues, peers, and our internal growth partners.

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
**Director of Development**


Phoenixville, PA

 **﻿Lead fundraising initiatives that create measurable community impact, strengthen donor relationships, and help our mission reach more people each year.**

 **Why You'll Love Working with Us**

* **Drive Meaningful Impact:** Help expand programs that empower individuals and families to move from crisis to stability throughout Lancaster and Chester Counties.
* **Build Lasting Relationships:** Cultivate meaningful connections with donors, community partners, and advocates whose generosity directly changes lives.
* **Shape Our Future:** Help guide the continued growth of a respected nonprofit organization.
* **Join a Supportive Team:** Collaborate with compassionate colleagues who celebrate one another, value teamwork, and are united by a shared commitment to serving the community.
* **Enjoy the Best of Both Worlds:** Bring your energy, passion, and development expertise to a growing organization where you can make a significant impact without the layers and stress often found in larger nonprofits.
* **Grow Your Career:** Take on a highly visible leadership role where your ideas, initiative, and fundraising expertise will make a lasting organizational impact while advancing your professional growth.

 **About Us**


Good Samaritan Services compassionately responds to individuals and families experiencing or at risk of homelessness across Lancaster and Chester Counties, walking alongside our neighbors as they move from crisis to stability through outreach, housing, and ongoing support. We believe lasting change happens through meaningful relationships, collaboration, and responsible stewardship, and we're committed to growing our impact so we can serve more people throughout the communities we call home.

 **What You'll Do as Our Director of Development**

* **Lead** annual fundraising initiatives, campaigns, special events, and development projects that advance our mission and achieve annual revenue goals.
* **Cultivate** and grow a portfolio of individual donors while identifying and engaging prospective major donors who are passionate about expanding our community impact.
* **Strengthen** donor relationships through thoughtful stewardship, personalized communication, and meaningful engagement that inspires long\-term support.

jobs.title: Turbo Tim's Chief Operating Officer / Integrator
jobs.description:
**Chief Operating Officer / Integrator**

**Turbo Tim’s Anything Automotive \| Twin Cities, Minnesota \| Compensation: $200,000–$300,000**

Turbo Tim’s is growing, and we need a COO who can help turn big ideas into a great company at scale.

I’m Turbo Tim. In EOS and *Rocket Fuel* terms, I’m the textbook Visionary. I see possibilities everywhere, move fast, and love trying things the automotive industry hasn’t tried. I need a true Integrator beside me: someone who loves people, brings clarity to complexity, makes decisions, builds strong leaders, and turns ideas into results. You’ll be empowered to lead the business and tell me when an idea needs a better plan.

We’re an independent, multi\-location automotive company built around **Cars, Cats, and Community**. We’re expanding quickly, building a YouTube channel that shows what shop life can be, and developing a software company aimed at improving this industry. Depending on your strengths and interests, you could help shape those ventures too. We put on community events like **Car Extravaganza** and **Crushawhirl**, and our team volunteers because giving back is part of who we are. There’s a lot happening here, and the right person will help us grow it without losing what makes it special.

Our values are **Care, CommUNITY, Trust, Innovation, and FUN**. They have to show up in how we treat customers, develop employees, solve problems, and make decisions. We take employee feedback seriously: we track eNPS, listen to what drives it, and keep changing how we work to make this a better place for our people.

**What you’ll own**

* Lead day\-to\-day operations across our locations and help build the systems, accountability, and leadership capacity needed for continued growth.
* Be the Integrator: turn vision into priorities, align the leadership team, follow through, and help us decide what deserves our attention now.
* Coach and grow our leaders. Build a company where people know what success looks like and have the support to reach it.
* Own operational performance and work with the team to improve the customer experience, financial results, and execution across the business.
* Use EOS tools and a healthy leadership cadence to surface issues, make decisions, and keep us moving.
* Protect and strengthen our culture as we add people, locations, and new ventures.

**You might be our person if**

* You’ve led people and operations through meaningful growth, and you can balance big\-picture thinking with consistent follow\-through.
* You understand EOS and the Visionary/Integrator relationship in *Rocket Fuel*, ideally because you’ve lived it.
* You’re direct, kind, calm under pressure, and genuinely good at getting the best out of people.
* You can challenge a passionate founder, earn trust across a team, and make ambitious ideas executable.
* You’re excited to bring a fresh perspective to automotive. **Experience outside the automotive industry is especially welcome.**
* You care about culture and employee feedback as much as you care about a scorecard.

Our previous COO has been an amazing Integrator and person. He set a high bar. At times we wondered how we could possibly offer him more room to grow, and he kept growing anyway. Those are big shoes to fill. You won’t be expected to fill them alone: we’ll support your development, give you room to lead, and expect you to invest just as deeply in the growth of our people.

If you want to lead a company that’s growing fast, trying new things, and doing real good in the community, we’d love to meet you. **Apply with your résumé and a short note about why the Visionary/Integrator partnership appeals to you.**

Pay: $200,000\.00 \- $275,000\.00 per year

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Vision insurance

**Company Overview**  
Bloomington Developmental Learning Center is a vibrant, multi\-cultural child care facility on the south east side of Bloomington, Indiana dedicated to nurturing each child that comes through our door. Through a play\-based curriculum, we foster emotional, social, and cognitive growth for children from six weeks to five years old.

**Job Overview**

The Executive Director administers and manages the high\-quality child care program at BDLC, a not\-for\-profit organization, which has been in existence for more than 50 years. The Director provides vision and leadership for staff, under the supervision of the Board of Directors, to meet long\-term goals and maintain the fiscal integrity of the Center. This role reports to the President of the Board.

The Executive Director has the following responsibilities:

**1\. Organizational Leadership \& Culture**

* **Vision and leadership:** Provide clear leadership and direction for the organization by setting priorities, aligning people and resources, and fostering a culture that supports children, families, staff, and the long\-term success of BDLC.
* **Communication, Collaboration \& Support:** Support staff and families in navigating concerns, challenges, and transitions; Foster open communication, collaboration, and mutual respect across the organization; Address conflicts constructively and help teams navigate difficult situations in a productive and professional manner; Partner with the Office Administrator and Curriculum Coordinators to align priorities, solve problems, and support staff and families.
* **Board, Family \& Community Engagement**: Build and maintain positive, professional relationships with families, Board members, and community partners; Partner with the Board by providing timely organizational updates, participating in Board meetings, and supporting effective governance and decision\-making; Build and maintain positive relationships with community partners, professional organizations, and the broader Bloomington community to support BDLC's mission and long\-term success.
* **Team Culture \& Staff Engagement**: Foster a positive, collaborative culture that supports staff retention, professional growth, and organizational success; Lead regular staff meetings to communicate priorities, organizational updates, and opportunities for feedback and discussion; Recognize staff contributions and create an environment where people feel valued, supported, and connected to BDLC's mission.

**2\. Operations \& Administration**

* **Program Operations \& Administrative Systems**: Oversee the day\-to\-day operations of the program, ensuring classrooms, facilities, and administrative systems operate effectively; Provide oversight and supervision of administrative systems and recordkeeping, ensuring required documentation and records are accurately maintained in accordance with BDLC policy and licensing requirements
* **Financial \& Enrollment Management:** In collaboration with BDLC’s finance committee, oversee program finances such as budgeting, purchasing, and financial reporting; Monitor enrollment and waitlist processes to support program capacity and financial stability
* **Policy \& Process Improvement**: In collaboration with the BDLC administrative team, implement program policies and procedures consistently, ensuring teachers and staff understand and follow established expectations; In collaboration with the BDLC board of directors, regularly evaluate program processes to identify opportunities for improvement

**3\. Staffing, Compliance \& Sustainability**

* **Hiring, Supervision, \& Performance Management**: Lead recruitment, hiring, onboarding, and training of qualified staff; Address performance concerns consistently and in accordance with BDLC’s policies and employment requirements; Create and monitor staffing schedules and classroom coverage to ensure appropriate ratios are consistently met; Partner with Curriculum Coordinators to develop, evaluate, and support staff as they grow into new roles and responsibilities.
* **Licensing \& Regulatory Compliance**: Maintain compliance with Indiana state licensing regulations, Paths to Quality standards, and BDLC policies; Monitor changes in Indiana state licensing regulations and communicate relevant changes to appropriate staff and the BDLC board of directors; Identify and address compliance concerns proactively
* **Strategic Planning \& Risk Management**: Anticipate future organizational needs and develop strategies that support continuity and stability; Identify emerging risks that may affect children, families, staff, finances, or BDLC’s ability to operate effectively; In collaboration with the BDLC board of directors, develop and maintain plans that support the long\-term stability and success of the program

As outlined by Indiana Licensing regulations, the Executive Director shall meet one (1\) of the following minimum education and experience qualifications:

(1\) A **bachelor of arts or bachelor of science degree** from an accredited college or university in **early childhood education** or **elementary education** with a kindergarten endorsement and grades of C or better.

(2\) **Any bachelor of arts or bachelor of science degree** from an accredited college or university must include one of the following: (A) **Fifteen credit hours in college level courses with documented content relating to the needs, skills, development, or teaching methods of children six years of age or younger and grades of C or better.** (B) **A CDA.**

(3\) **A two year associate’s degree in early childhood education from an accredited college or university, with a grade of C or better and a minimum of three years of experience in an early childhood program.**

jobs.description:
Posting Details
  
  

INTERVIEWS ARE ANTICIPATED TO BE CONDUCTED WITHIN TWO WEEKS OF CLOSING DATE
  
  

Please visit us at www.IndianArtsandCulture.org
  
  

Created in 1978 by the New Mexico Legislature, the Department of Cultural Affairs represents New Mexico's dedication to preserving and celebrating the cultural integrity and diversity of our state. The Department oversees a broad range of New Mexico's arts and cultural heritage agencies. These include 15 divisions representing a variety of programs and services.
  
Why does the job exist?
  
  

The Museum of Indian Arts and Culture (MIAC) is a center of stewardship, knowledge, and understanding of the artistic, cultural, and intellectual achievements of the diverse Indigenous peoples of the Greater Southwest. MIAC's mission is achieved by inspiring the public to learn more about the vibrant cultures of the Southwest, caring for and interpreting the collection, and collaboration with the Indigenous people of the Southwest. The Deputy Director assists the Executive Director in the administrative and strategic operation of the museum, including the Laboratory of Anthropology, Center for New Mexico Archaeology (CNMA), and Museum Hill Cafe.
  
How does it get done?
  
  

The Deputy Director oversees operations of the Museum, Library of Laboratory of Anthropology, and the Archaeological Repository at the CNMA. Responsibilities span a wide range of activities including, but not limited to, strategic planning, grant and annual budget preparation, preservation of and access to collections, security and visitor services, human resources and personnel policies, and management of facilities including planning maintenance and coordinating repairs. Projects are completed through close collaboration with other Department of Cultural Affairs bureaus and partners, including Facility Management Bureau, Museum Resources Division, and Museum of New Mexico Foundation. The Deputy Director represents the Museum to the public, Museum members, associated foundations, and the State of New Mexico in the Director's absence and as delegated by the Director with all the constituencies affiliated with the Museum.
  
Who are the customers?
  
  

Museum visitors include local, national, and international learners of all ages. MIAC seeks to be an inclusive and accessible museum that welcomes all of our public. Through continued collaboration, MIAC has maintained and strengthened relationships with members of the 23 tribes located in New Mexico's nineteen Pueblos, three Apache Tribes, and the Navajo Nation, as well as native nations in Colorado, Arizona and Texas. After nearly 100 years since the founding of the Laboratory of Anthropology, MIAC has a passionate community of supporters.
  
Ideal Candidate
  
  

Museum visitors include local, national, and international learners of all ages. MIAC seeks to be an inclusive and accessible museum that welcomes all of our public. Through continued collaboration, MIAC has maintained and strengthened relationships with members of the 23 tribes located in New Mexico's nineteen Pueblos, three Apache Tribes, and the Navajo Nation, as well as native nations in Colorado, Arizona and Texas. After nearly 100 years since the founding of the Laboratory of Anthropology, MIAC has a passionate community of supporters.
  
Minimum Qualification
  
  

Bachelor's Degree in a relevant field of study from an accredited college or university and nine (9\) years of professional level experience operating within parameters and guidelines directly related to the purpose of the position defined by the agency at the time of recruitment. Any combination of education from an accredited college or university and/or direct experience in this occupation totaling thirteen (13\) years may substitute for the required education and experience. A hiring agency will designate a portion of the required experience to include supervisory and/or specialized experience. Any required licensure, certification or registration shall be defined at the time of recruitment and will be in addition to the above requirements.
  
Employment Requirements
  
  

Employment is subject to a pre\-employment background investigation and is conditional pending results. Must possess and maintain a current Defensive Driving Course Certificate from the State of New Mexico or must pass and receive Defensive Driving Course Certification as a condition of continued employment. Must possess and maintain a valid Driver's License.
  
Working Conditions
  
  

Work is performed in an office setting with exposure to Visual/Video Display Terminal (VDT) and dust. There is regular interaction with the public. Extensive computer and phone use and extended periods of standing, walking, and lifting. Must be able to lift up to 40 lbs.

jobs.description:
Position Summary:
The University of Arizona Foundation is seeking a motivated and goal\-oriented fundraising professional to join the Philanthropy and Alumni Engagement team as Senior Director of Development (Senior DOD) for College of Architecture, Life \& Environmental Sciences (CALES). The Senior Director will lead efforts to secure major and principal gifts of $50,000 or more in support of the goals and objectives of the College, as well as design and implement fundraising strategies that will generate revenue and drive the growth of the College’s mission.  

The Senior DOD will be a key member of the development team reporting to the Associate Vice President, Development. This position is a member of the Philanthropy Alumni and Engagement Team (PAE) and subject to joint management by the University of Arizona and the University of Arizona Foundation as specified in the restated Development Services and Asset Management Agreement dated July 2, 2021\.  

Supervisory Responsibility:
The Senior DOD will be accountable for providing strategic leadership and oversight, performance planning and evaluation, staff training and development, recruitment, and may contribute to recommending pay decisions for their direct reports. The Senior Director is expected to devote 70% of work time to major gift fundraising activities and 30% of work time to management and administrative responsibilities.  

Essential Functions/Major Responsibilities:

* Serve as the lead development professional for CALES.
* Partner with department heads, center directors, and other administrators on fundraising.
* Advise the Dean of the College and President of the University of Arizona Foundation or designee on all College development activities.
* Participate with the Dean and the College’s departments in the strategic planning of new projects and initiatives.
* Develop and sustain strong relationships with the College’s faculty, board members, alumni, volunteers, donors, and financial professionals and other relevant stakeholders.
* Build and manage a portfolio of 50–70 qualified prospects, including individuals, foundations, and select corporations with 40\-50 in cultivation/solicitation; 40% of those in cultivation/solicitation capacity are rated at $250K\+ and 15% are rated at $1M\+.
* After an initial 6\-month onboarding period, execute an agreed\-upon metric of at least 100 current or prospect donor visits and the successful closure of 15\+ major/principal gift proposals per year, with an expectation of $3M\+ raised after the initial onboarding period (with incremental increases after the first year).
* Plan, coordinate, and schedule weekly personal visits with prospects and donors utilizing UAF software, introductory letters, emails/texts, and phone calls to set appointments.
* Direct and manage the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of major and principal gift level individuals, corporate and foundation prospects to support all department capital and program goals.
* Develop personalized strategies for all assigned donors and prospects which builds, maintains, and enhances relationships while furthering donors’ philanthropic objectives.
* Within 6 weeks of hire deliver a strategic development plan to VP and Dean.
* Assist PAE leadership in determining staffing needs, making hiring decisions, and working to onboard new development team members.
* Supervise development staff, including hiring, mentoring, and performance management.
* Oversee an annual giving program with a national outreach to support college goals.
* In partnership with PAE, provide a high level of support in stewardship and recognition efforts for annual giving donors.
* Provide input and direction for development\-focused newsletters, invitations, brochures, and other publications/communications, as needed.
* Design and manage solicitation and stewardship plans in Lynx to support fundraising initiatives.
* Maintain current and accurate records of donor prospects recorded in UAF software. On a weekly basis, enter contact reports of all visits, significant telephone conversations, letters and correspondence, gift solicitations, and other communications with donors. Maintain information about current and future gift proposals (asks).
* Ensure all contributions are properly documented and handled in accordance with the University of Arizona Gift Policy.
* Partner with College and PAE alumni engagement colleagues to help build donor pipeline for the College.
* Creatively leverage outreach activities (e.g. tours, lectures, exhibits, etc.) to develop new major gift prospects.
* Utilize the UA Foundation’s CRM (Lynx) to record donor interactions, proposals, and activity in a timely, accurate manner.
* Partner with colleagues across PAE (e.g., Gift Planning, Annual Giving, Marketing \& Communications, Prospect Development) to ensure integrated donor engagement and maximize fundraising impact.
* Partner with colleagues and promote a culture of philanthropy across the University and work effectively as part of the greater PAE.
* Represent the College, University, and PAE at public events, including delivering remarks.
* Other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:* Commitment to working in a collaborative team environment with shared goals.
* Ability to work efficiently with a wide variety of individuals, including donors, PAE colleagues, deans, faculty and staff.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

The Minnesota Association of Independent Schools (MAIS) is made up of seventeen private, independent schools accredited by the Independent Schools Association of the Central States (ISACS).


Our Mission is to support and connect Independent Schools in Minnesota by:


* Working to foster and preserve the independence and freedom of choice in education
* Providing a forum for professional development and the exchange of ideas among faculty and staff

Promoting the features and benefits of Independent Schools to prospective families and employees

This is a part time position (15\-20 hours per week), with the exact hours varying depending on the week. This position reports to the MAIS President.

**DIRECTOR OF ADVOCACY AND EXTERNAL AFFAIRS**


Jericho Road Community Health Center is actively seeking a **Director of Advocacy \& External Affairs**. This position is full\-time, within the Advancement Department, working at our 233 W Ferry location.

**Work with a Purpose**


Jericho Road Community Health Center offers the opportunity to engage in a movement far larger than any one individual. We believe that we can all be people with positive influence. We influence each other, our clients and patients, our families and communities. We are part of a global team that influences the health and wellbeing of communities internationally. Every day, Jericho Road’s mission of caring for communities and advocating for systemic health equity guides us in our collective purpose. We are looking for individuals who share that goal and are committed to that service. As a federally qualified health center (FQHC), our organization’s mission is deeply rooted in making fundamental changes in the communities we serve, advocating for social justice and meeting people where they are. With global clinics across the world, the impact you make will transcend borders, with opportunities to engage in meaningful work at our Sierra Leone, Goma or Nepal global clinics.

**Why Jericho:** Jericho Road offers competitive pay and benefits including medical (single\-high coverage paid in full by employer), HSA, dental, vision, employer paid life insurance benefit, supplemental insurances, tuition discounts, generous paid time off, the opportunity for global travel to our three global health clinics, and loan forgiveness for applicable positions. Jericho Road values both work and life. The option of a flexible 40\-hour workweek is possible within certain teams.

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and lead the organization's annual advocacy agenda in collaboration with executive leadership, providers, service teams, and staff.
* Monitor local, state, and federal policy developments affecting community health, immigrant communities, housing, and social determinants of health.
* Represent Jericho Road in advocacy coalitions and partner networks, including organizations such as CHCANYS, NYIC, NACHC, PPG, PCDC, Lead Safety Taskforce, Housing Access NY, and other relevant partnerships.
* Organize and coordinate advocacy campaigns that advance strategic priorities through meetings with elected officials, coalition actions, public testimony, press events, digital advocacy efforts, and constituent engagement.
* Develop and maintain relationships with elected officials, government agencies, and key community stakeholders.
* Coordinate site visits, tours, and educational opportunities for policymakers and community leaders.
* Represent the organization through public speaking engagements, educational presentations, panel discussions, and community events.
* Serve as the primary coordinator for media inquiries and public relations opportunities, including drafting and overseeing press releases, media statements, and public messaging
* Support the coordination of community outreach opportunities, including tabling and participation in relevant external events.
* Build and strengthen relationships with community organizations, educational institutions, healthcare partners, and other stakeholders.

* Ensure organizational communications consistently reflect Jericho Road's mission, values, brand standards, and voice.

* Lead planning and coordination of advocacy\-related events, including activities associated with National Health Center Week.
* Coordinate engagement opportunities with elected officials, policymakers, and community stakeholders.

* Directly supervise the marketing and communications functions of the organization
* Recruit, train, supervise, and mentor interns supporting advocacy, communications, marketing, or public engagement initiatives.

jobs.title: Director of Communications & Public Engagement
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**
---------------------


This position is a 1\.0 FTE appointment serving the School Architecture and Design at the University of Kansas.
  

Working in collaboration with the Dean and the leadership team of the School, the position oversees all communications and marketing initiatives for the School and its units to translate complex students, alumni, faculty and staff achievements and impacts into clear, compelling narratives that improve student enrollment, retention, engagement and success; support advancement and fundraising; and promote reputation and community excellence.
  

The position is a member of the Dean’s leadership team. The position liaises with KU Marketing and Public Affairs, and KU Endowment Association on matters related to communications and public engagement. The position supervises the Graphic Designer of the School and a staff of student employees. The Position serves at the pleasure of the Dean and reports to the Dean.
**Job Description**
-------------------


**Responsibilities Related to Strategic Communications (90%)**
  

Strategic leadership responsibilities:
* Works with the Dean and the leadership team of the School to develop and implement an integrated strategic communications plan to advance the School’s brand and increase awareness of its programs, activities, and mission. The plan will identify priority audiences, messages, channels, responsibilities, an editorial schedule, and measures of success.
* Works directly and regularly with Department Chairs to understand departmental priorities, upcoming initiatives, events, accomplishments, recruitment needs, and opportunities for communication and promotion. Meets with the Chairs collectively or individually at least four times each academic year( twice per semester) to maintain consistent communication between the departments and the School’s communications efforts.

jobs.description:
**Location:** New Hope, PA / Titusville, NJ, with travel throughout Bucks (PA), Hunterdon (NJ), Mercer (NJ), and Montgomery (PA) Counties

**Reports to:** Board of Directors \| Status: Full\-time, Exempt

**Start Date:** January 1, 2027

**About Rolling Harvest Food Rescue**

Since 2010, Rolling Harvest Food Rescue has connected local farms' fresh, healthy surplus produce to food\- and nutrition\-insecure residents throughout Bucks County, PA and neighboring counties. Through farm\-based gleaning, produce rescue, growing, and distribution programs, Rolling Harvest partners with dozens of local growers and dozens of hunger\-relief sites — including food pantries, community kitchens, shelters, and low\-income senior housing — to deliver fresh produce free of charge. The nonprofit organization also facilitates nutrition education and awareness of food insecurity, food waste, and sustainable agriculture. Rolling Harvest envisions an equitable, local, and sustainable food system in which abundant access to fresh, healthy food is a fundamental right, not a privilege.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director (ED) is the chief executive officer of Rolling Harvest Food Rescue and works in partnership with the Board of Directors to advance the organization's mission. The ED provides strategic leadership, oversees daily operations, manages staff and volunteers, leads fundraising and development, and serves as the primary public face of the organization. This is an opportunity for a mission\-driven leader to guide a well\-established, respected grassroots nonprofit through its next stage of growth and impact.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide visionary leadership and translate the Board's strategic priorities into an actionable operating plan.
* Oversee broad operational objectives, including gleaning, growing, and food rescue goals, Food Access Hub management, and special distributions. Engage in daily operations when needed.
* Recruit, supervise, and support a small paid team along with a large volunteer base.
* Lead fundraising efforts, individual donor cultivation, corporate partnerships, and special events. Assist the Deputy Director with grant writing and reporting.
* Support the Procurement \& Volunteer Manager with maintaining and growing relationships with partner farms and hunger\-relief agencies across Bucks, Hunterdon, Mercer, and Montgomery Counties.
* Manage the annual budget and ensure sound financial and administrative practices in partnership with the Board of Directors and Bookkeeper.
* Serve as the primary spokesperson with media, government officials, and community partners. Oversee all social media messaging.
* Report regularly to the Board of Directors and support Board development and governance.
* Champion the organization's nutrition education and food\-waste awareness initiatives.

**Qualifications**

* 5\+ years of nonprofit management, hunger\-relief, agricultural, or related community\-impact experience involving strategic planning; direct executive leadership experience preferred
* Strong interpersonal skills, ability to manage others and build collaborations
* Ability to handle multiple responsibilities, prioritize work, solve problems, and operate under time and work volume pressure
* Demonstrated success in fundraising, grant writing, major gifts, and donor cultivation
* Strong financial management skills, including budgeting and nonprofit financial oversight
* Experience building and maintaining partnerships and relationships with diverse stakeholders — farmers, hunger relief organizations, volunteers, funders, and legislators
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills; dynamic energy with an ability to speak publicly
* Familiarity with, and passion for RHFR’s mission, including food systems, agriculture, food recovery, and hunger\-relief work
* Commitment to building an inclusive organization and working with a diverse community
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
* Valid driver's license is required given regional travel

**Compensation \& Benefits** 

Compensation ranges from $80,000 to $90,000 commensurate with experience and education. Benefits include a health care stipend if needed, five weeks paid vacation, five PTO days, nine holidays, cell phone and home office allowances, and mileage reimbursement for regional travel. This position is a combination of remote and field\-based work. Your schedule will fluctuate throughout the year based on seasonal demands and specific events.

**To Apply**

Please submit a cover letter, resume, and three professional references to . Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis beginning September 23, 2026\. Rolling Harvest Food Rescue is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our organization.

Pay: $80,000\.00 \- $90,000\.00 per year

**Position Summary**

This role works closely with the Chief Development Officer to execute effective fundraising strategies that fuel our programs and support survivors. The DoD will manage donor communications, write grant proposals to government and private funders, cultivate and steward event sponsors, support event planning, and contribute to campaigns that uplift survivor stories and community impact.

Success in this role means building authentic donor relationships, meeting deadlines, and contributing creative ideas that inspire generosity and deepen engagement, all while helping create a safer, more supportive world for survivors and their families.

* Oversee the donor CRM, ensuring efficient, consistent use across the team

new_jobs.title: JPL Deputy Director
new_jobs.description:
The Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), a federally funded research and development center managed by the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) for NASA, is seeking an exceptional executive leader to serve as its Deputy Director/Chief Operating Officer and help shape the future of one of the world's premier aerospace and research institutions, enabling groundbreaking discoveries, advancing national priorities, and supporting missions that expand humanity's understanding of Earth, the solar system, and the universe. Partnering closely with the Director, the Deputy Director will provide strategic leadership, institutional stewardship, and operational excellence across a complex enterprise of scientific, engineering, and administrative functions. The successful candidate will empower a world\-class workforce while strengthening the partnerships, capabilities, and organizational resilience necessary to achieve JPL's ambitious mission now and into the future.

#### **Job Summary**


The Deputy Director of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory is appointed by the Vice President/ Director of JPL with the concurrence of the President of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), which manages JPL for NASA, and in consultation with the NASA Administrator.


Reporting to the JPL Director, the Deputy Director serves as the Laboratory's Chief Operating Officer, providing executive leadership for institutional operations and mission execution. The Deputy Director leads and integrates the Executive Council, drives organizational execution and accountability, and provides strategic leadership for the Laboratory's workforce. As a strategic partner to the Director, the Deputy Director orchestrates cross\-functional coordination among Business, Operations, and Programmatic leadership while maintaining institutional alignment and operational continuity. The Deputy Director ensures operational excellence, fosters a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement, and engages in strategic relationships with NASA, Caltech, the Department of War, Intelligence Community, and Space Force. Through integrated execution across programmatic and institutional functions, the Deputy Director ensures operational excellence across all Laboratory functions, driving continuous improvement while deepening the critical Caltech\-JPL partnership.

#### **Key Responsibilities**

### **Executive Leadership**

* Provide executive leadership and ensure integration of the Laboratory's institutional operations, which includes acquisitions, workforce management, infrastructure, facilities, and administrative organizations.
* Partner with the JPL Director to establish institutional priorities, execute strategic initiatives, and advance the Laboratory's long\-term vision.
* Continue to strengthen and advance the close and enduring partnership with Caltech
* Serve as Acting Director, when delegated, exercising full authority for Laboratory operations and executive decision\-making.
* Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, integrity, and continuous improvement.
* Support and partner with the Director in leading the Laboratory through periods of organizational change while maintaining workforce engagement, operational continuity, and mission success.
* Chair the weekly Executive Council, facilitating Laboratory\-wide decision\-making, policy development, and organizational alignment.

### **Strategic Institutional Leadership**

* Assume a leadership role in the development and execution of JPL's long\-range institutional strategy, which includes aligning workforce, infrastructure, technology investments, and operational capabilities with future mission needs. Ensure Executive Council alignment on institutional strategy and drive integrated execution across programmatic and institutional functions.
* Initiate organizational assessments and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance institutional effectiveness.
* Oversee Laboratory\-level governance, management systems, and enterprise decision making processes to ensure transparency, accountability, compliance, and organizational performance.
* Deepen the enduring partnership with Caltech administration, participating in Caltech Board of Trustees engagements concerning JPL.

### **Programmatic Oversight**

* Chair Center Project Management Reviews (PMR) to evaluate mission readiness, risk posture, and programmatic execution across all spaceflight and scientific projects.
* Serve as JPL's senior representative to the NASA Office of JPL Management and Oversight (NOJMO), while acting as the primary institutional liaison with NASA and Caltech functional leadership.
* Ensure effective integration of mission, compliance, and institutional functions across the organization.
* With the Director, lead JPL's strategic relationships with the Department of War, the Intelligence Community, and the U.S. Space Force, serving as the primary executive interface for national security programs.

### **Institutional Processes and Operations**

* Facilitate cross\-functional coordination among Business, Operations, and Programmatic leadership to drive aligned execution and resolve cross\-functional institutional challenges.
* Ensure clear governance and escalation paths that empower functional leaders while maintaining institutional cohesion.
* Chair the Laboratory's Emergency Policy Committee (EPC) and lead the emergency preparedness, crisis response, and continuity of operations framework.
* Serve as the Laboratory’s Responsible Official for the South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD).
* Provide executive oversight of the Ethics, Ombuds, Office of Safety and Mission Success Offices.
* Champion executive talent development, succession planning, leadership development, while establishing and maintaining clear performance standards and accountability for Executive Council members and their organizations.

**Position:** VP, Director of Development – Cleveland

**Type: Full\-time, exempt**  


**Who We Are**  


Partnership Schools is accepting applications for the role of VP, Director of Development – Cleveland in Cleveland, OH. The ideal candidate brings zeal, creativity, imagination, positivity, and passion to their work and is ready to dive into a fast\-paced and exciting entrepreneurial environment.  


Since 2013, the Partnership has been a pioneering school management organization shaping the next generation of urban Catholic schooling. From 2013 through 2024, the Archdiocese of New York granted operational management of seven long\-standing Pre\-K to 8th\-grade schools in the South Bronx and Harlem to the Partnership, and during that time the schools experienced substantial math and reading achievement gains and increased enrollment significantly. In 2020, the Partnership was invited to expand to the Diocese of Cleveland, where it manages five schools in the heart of the city providing students in historically underserved neighborhoods with the academic preparation, faith formation, values, and skills they need to thrive. The Partnership currently serves about 1,000 students in Cleveland, nearly all of whom live in poverty. In July 2026, the Partnership expanded its mission to Toledo, Ohio, adding two schools to its network and extending its commitment to strengthening urban Catholic education in new communities. As the Partnership begins the 2026\-2027 school year, it continues to build on its proven model of academic excellence, faith\-based formation, and transformative support for students and families.  


The historic success of urban Catholic schools stems not only from a rigorous tradition of academic excellence but also from an emphasis on developing self\-worth, moral character, a love of learning, and a sense of civic responsibility—all part of our long\-standing commitment to educating the whole child. Partnership Schools is unique in knitting this tradition together with lessons from high\-achieving public, charter, and independent schools, in the service of our students.  


At the Partnership, we believe all children can achieve at the highest levels. If you are interested in serving as a pioneer in education and share an unwavering commitment to raising student achievement and an appreciation and respect for Catholic culture, identity, and values, we want to hear from you!

In our first decade, Partnership Schools successfully pioneered a groundbreaking approach for the independent management of urban Catholic schools, one needed now more than ever. As Catholic schools nationally have faced enrollment, academic, and financial crises that resulted in waves of closures, the schools in the Partnership increased enrollment, produced academic growth, and raised more money than ever. Because our effective model serves as a proof\-point of what is possible, Partnership Schools is accelerating our growth and tenaciously expanding philanthropy to increase the number of students served and bolster the organization’s national impact on the school choice movement.  

Partnership Schools seeks an entrepreneurial and experienced VP, Director of Development – Cleveland to help catalyze the organization’s continued growth and advancement.
